sphere-2-3.title: The complex Hopf map
sphere-2-3.summary: The first genuinely surprising homotopy group of spheres. Its generator is represented by the Hopf fibration S³ → S².
sphere-2-3.interestingBecause: A higher-dimensional sphere maps essentially onto a lower-dimensional one.

sphere-4-7.title: The quaternionic Hopf map
sphere-4-7.summary: Its infinite summand is generated by the quaternionic Hopf fibration S⁷ → S⁴.
sphere-4-7.interestingBecause: It combines an infinite Hopf class with finite torsion.

sphere-8-15.title: The octonionic Hopf map
sphere-8-15.summary: The last classical Hopf fibration contributes the infinite summand of π₁₅(S⁸).
sphere-8-15.interestingBecause: It is tied to the exceptional algebra of the octonions.

stable-0.title: Degree
stable-0.summary: The zeroth stable stem is infinite cyclic and records the degree of a stable self-map of a sphere.
stable-0.interestingBecause: It is the unit from which stable composition begins.

stable-1.title: The first stable stem
stable-1.summary: The stable class η has order two and is detected geometrically by suspensions of the complex Hopf map.
stable-1.interestingBecause: The first positive stable stem is already nontrivial.

stable-3.title: The third stable stem
stable-3.summary: The stable class ν generates a cyclic group of order 24.
stable-3.interestingBecause: Its 2- and 3-primary pieces combine into a cyclic group of order 24.

stable-7.title: The seventh stable stem
stable-7.summary: The stable class σ generates a cyclic group of order 240.
stable-7.interestingBecause: Its order 240 reflects 2-, 3-, and 5-primary information at once.
